question.text: What distinguishes an ETF (Exchange Traded Fund) from an Index Fund?

answer.text: ETFs are actively managed while Index Funds are passively managed
ETFs track a benchmark index while Index Funds do not
ETFs are listed on a stock exchange and have real-time NAV, while Index Funds are not listed and have daily NAV
ETFs have a higher expense ratio than Index Funds

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook's comparison of ETFs and index funds, both are passive funds that track a benchmark index. The distinguishing feature highlighted is that ETFs are listed and traded on a stock exchange with a real-time NAV, while index funds are not exchange-traded and transact at the end-of-day NAV like other open-ended mutual funds. The Trap: Option A is wrong because both ETFs and index funds are passive, not active. Option B is wrong because both track an index. Option D contradicts the workbook framing of the listed/real-time NAV versus daily-NAV distinction as the key difference. Note: The checked source pages frame the comparison around the listing/NAV mechanics. Claims about ETFs having a lower expense ratio or requiring a demat account/broker, while commonly stated elsewhere, are not drawn from these pages.
